templates.pattern: A cyclist travels a distance of [D] km in [T] hours. Calculate the average speed of the cyclist.
templates.explanation:
Average speed = Distance ÷ Time
= [D] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] km/h

Always divide total distance by total time to find average speed.

templates.pattern: A train travels at a constant speed of [S] km/h for [T] hours. Calculate the total distance travelled by the train.
templates.explanation:
Distance = Speed × Time
= [S] × [T]
= [RESULT] km

When speed is constant, simply multiply speed by time.

templates.pattern: A car travels [D] km at a constant speed of [S] km/h. Calculate the time taken for the journey. Give your answer in hours.
templates.explanation:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
= [D] ÷ [S]
= [RESULT] hours

Rearrange the speed formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time becomes Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

templates.pattern: A motorbike accelerates from [U] m/s to [V] m/s in [T] seconds. Calculate the acceleration of the motorbike.
templates.explanation:
Acceleration = (Final velocity - Initial velocity) ÷ Time
= ([V] - [U]) ÷ [T]
= [V-U] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] m/s²

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

templates.pattern: A resultant force of [F] N acts on an object of mass [M] kg. Calculate the acceleration produced.
templates.explanation:
Using Newton's Second Law: F = ma
Rearranging: a = F ÷ m
= [F] ÷ [M]
= [RESULT] m/s²

Force is measured in newtons (N), mass in kg and acceleration in m/s².

templates.pattern: A football of mass [M] kg is moving at [V] m/s. Calculate the kinetic energy of the football.
templates.explanation:
Kinetic Energy = ½ × mass × velocity²
= 0.5 × [M] × [V]²
= 0.5 × [M] × [V*V]
= [RESULT] J

Kinetic energy depends on the square of velocity, so doubling speed quadruples KE.

templates.pattern: A box of mass [M] kg is lifted to a height of [H] m above the ground. Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained by the box. (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation:
Gravitational Potential Energy = mass × g × height
= [M] × 10 × [H]
= [RESULT] J

GPE increases with mass and height. g = 10 m/s² is used at GCSE level.

templates.pattern: A person pushes a shopping trolley with a force of [F] N over a distance of [D] m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done by the person.
templates.explanation:
Work Done = Force × Distance
= [F] × [D]
= [RESULT] J

Work is done only when a force causes movement in the direction of the force. One joule = one newton-metre.

templates.pattern: An electric motor does [W] J of work in [T] seconds. Calculate the power output of the motor.
templates.explanation:
Power = Work Done ÷ Time
= [W] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] W

Power is measured in watts (W). 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

templates.pattern: An astronaut has a mass of [M] kg. Calculate the weight of the astronaut on Earth. (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation:
Weight = mass × gravitational field strength
= [M] × 10
= [RESULT] N

Weight is a force measured in newtons. Mass is measured in kg and never changes. Weight changes depending on the gravitational field strength.
